report.title: NYJ at MIA: Week 12 Scouting Report
report.summary: The Jets lean on short, quick passes and yards after catch, and their run defense is the soft spot Miami can attack. Their pressure comes mostly from the blitz, so protection and quick throws matter on early downs. Third down and the red zone are areas to press, while special teams favor Miami's returners against a weak Jets punt unit.

sections.heading: Opponent offense
sections.body: NYJ drops back on 52.6% [oc1] of 500 early-down plays [oc2], but distance drives the split: 28.7% [oc3] passing on 94 short-yardage plays [oc4] versus 65.7% [oc6] on 428 long-distance plays [oc7]. Pass EPA is 0.05 [oc10] on 381 plays [oc11], ranking 17th [oc12], and run EPA is -0.04 [oc13], also 17th [oc15]. Expect a short-passing, yards-after-catch offense with a 7.8 yards [oc18] average depth of target on 332 attempts [oc19]. Explosives come more from runs (10.8% [oc20]) than passes (7.9% [oc21]). Designed runs go left 35.3% [oc22] and middle 28.6% [oc23]. Play action is 20.7% [oc24] of dropbacks and motion shows on 50.4% [oc25] of plays. Miami's blitz rate ranks 30th [oc32] with a 15.0% [oc29] pressure proxy, so Miami seldom sends extra rushers and motion and play action are the likely tools against that light-blitz front.

sections.heading: Opponent defense
sections.body: The Jets allow 0.07 EPA per play [dc1], 28th in the league [dc3], and their run defense is the soft spot: 48.5% [dc4] of runs gain positive EPA on 305 plays [dc5], and 10.8% [dc6] go 10+ yards. Against the pass they allow 49.2% success [dc8] on 366 dropbacks [dc9], with 7.9% [dc10] of passes going 20+ yards, so there are no obvious deep-ball holes. Pressure comes mostly from the blitz: 36.6% [dc11] of dropbacks see 5+ rushers, 6th highest in the league [dc12]. The Jets stack the box, averaging 6.7 [dc16] defenders on runs, 10th highest [dc17]. Miami's run success is 34.9% [dc18] versus 39.2% [dc20] passing, so the early-down edge is more likely through the air. Third down is a weakness at 43.5% [dc22] allowed on 131 plays [dc23], ranking 23rd [dc24]. The red zone has allowed touchdowns on 71.1% [dc25] of 38 drives [dc26].

sections.heading: Special teams
sections.body: J. Sanders has made 27 [kc1] of 30 [kc2] field goals, 90.0% [kc3], but is 71.4% [kc4] from 50-plus on just 7 [kc5] tries, so trust him in mid-range and treat long attempts as a real miss risk. The punting is the weak spot: a 42.3 [kc6] net average on 38 [kc7] punts, with 31.6% [kc8] of kicks pinning Miami inside the 20. Kickoff touchbacks are 17.2% [kc9] on 58 [kc10] kickoffs, so Miami's returners will usually start in ordinary field position. NYJ's coverage allows 26.6 [kc11] yards per return on 44 [kc12] returns, while Miami's returners average 26.1 [kc13] on 49 [kc14]. Overall special-teams EPA is 0.01 [kc15] per play for NYJ over 288 [kc16] plays and -0.12 [kc17] for Miami on 241 [kc18]. Late with a lead, kick away from the Jets' return unit only when the margin is safe; otherwise Miami's returners can gain field position off the weak punting.

sections.heading: Injuries and availability
sections.body: Jets DT David Onyemata is listed Out with an abdomen injury, but his absence is hard to read given a small sample of 2 games [ic4]. WRs Omar Cooper Jr. and Isaiah Williams are also listed Out with ankle and rib injuries, and they account for 7.5% [ic7] and 6.9% [ic8] of Jets targets over 318 targets [ic9]. Expect that volume to shift to the remaining receivers, backs and tight ends, and expect a more run-leaning interior. On the Miami side, S Dante Trader Jr. is Doubtful with a shoulder injury after 9 games [ic12] as a regular back-end piece, so Miami loses a dependable player at safety.

sections.heading: Key matchups
sections.body: First, blitz protection: NYJ sends five-plus rushers on 36.6% [mc1] of dropbacks, 6th highest in the league [mc2], and Miami's pressure proxy allowed is 16.7% [mc3] on 329 dropbacks [mc4]. Keep a back in on early downs and get the ball out quickly on hot throws. Second, the run game: NYJ allows positive EPA on 48.5% [mc5] of runs over 305 plays [mc6] and averages 6.7 [mc8] defenders in the box, yet Miami's run success is 34.9% [mc9] on 232 carries [mc10]. With Onyemata out (46.0% [mc11] snap share across 2 games [mc12]), attack the interior and use play action to pull the box out of run fits. Third, money downs: NYJ allows 43.5% [mc15] third-down conversions, 23rd in the league [mc16], and touchdowns on 71.1% [mc17] of 38 [mc18] red zone drives, so prioritize the pass there. Fourth, the back end: with Cooper (7.5% [mc19]) and Williams (6.9% [mc20]) of Jets targets out, Miami's Dante Trader Jr. is Doubtful after an 85.2% [mc21] snap share across 9 games [mc22], so plan coverage for the remaining Jets receivers and tight ends with a backup safety on the field.
